cancer_indication: HER2-overexpressing (HER2+) breast cancer in both early (adjuvant/neoadjuvant) and metastatic settings.
moa: Trastuzumab binds the extracellular domain of the HER2 (ERBB2) receptor on tumor cells, causing receptor downmodulation and blockade of downstream signaling. This inhibits proliferative pathways (MAPK/ERK, PI3K/AKT) and induces cell-cycle arrest (including via p27^Kip1 upregulation). Through its Fc region, it recruits immune effector mechanisms by engaging Fcγ receptors on immune cells to mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) against HER2+ tumor cells. It has also been shown to inhibit tumor angiogenesis.

REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.description: Represents oncogenic HER2 (ERBB2) receptor signaling driven by HER2 overexpression/amplification, including receptor activation and downstream proliferative/survival signaling outputs.
REACTOME_CONSTITUTIVE_SIGNALING_BY_OVERE.interpretation: HER2-driven signaling is a key dependency in HER2-amplified breast cancer and is the central disease driver that trastuzumab targets at the receptor level.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: HER2 (ERBB2) amplification/overexpression drives oncogenic signaling (oncogene addiction), creating a direct target for trastuzumab and predicting clinical benefit.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Despite high ERBB2 signaling, resistance can occur via impaired antibody access/processing (e.g., p95HER2, MUC4 masking) or strong downstream bypass signaling that makes growth less HER2-dependent.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: Low ERBB2 signaling generally indicates lack of the therapeutic target for trastuzumab in breast cancer (outside of HER2-amplified/overexpressed disease).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: HER2-non-amplified tumors have insufficient ERBB2 target engagement, so trastuzumab is ineffective.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab blocks HER2 signaling and promotes receptor down-modulation, reducing ERBB2-driven proliferative/survival signaling and yielding tumor control when dependence is high.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Even if ERBB2 pathway activity falls, tumors can persist through downstream PI3K activation (e.g., PTEN loss) or alternate RTKs, producing resistance despite HER2 blockade.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Immune-mediated killing can dominate; inflammatory/stress responses may transiently elevate HER2-pathway transcripts while Fc-mediated clearance still produces sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Compensatory HER family/RTK signaling or selection for HER2 signaling reactivation under drug pressure can raise ERBB2 pathway signatures and mark acquired resistance.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Core survival and growth signaling axis downstream of receptor tyrosine kinases, integrating PI3K, AKT, and mTOR activity to promote proliferation and resistance to cell death.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity is a major determinant of tumor survival in HER2+ breast cancer and is highlighted as a critical bypass/resistance axis when it remains active despite HER2 blockade.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: If PI3K activity is primarily driven downstream of HER2 with intact PTEN control, trastuzumab can still suppress HER2→PI3K flux and remain effective.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Constitutive PI3K activation (e.g., PTEN loss/PIK3CA mutations) reduces reliance on HER2 signaling and is a well-described mechanism of trastuzumab resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low baseline PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling implies fewer downstream bypass routes, increasing dependence on HER2-driven signaling and likelihood of response.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may be HER2-driven via parallel pathways (e.g., MAPK) or have PK/immune limitations, leading to non-response even with low PI3K signaling.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab can reduce PI3K/AKT signaling via HER2 blockade and PTEN-dependent mechanisms, contributing to growth inhibition and response.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: If PI3K/AKT falls but MAPK or EMT/STAT3 programs sustain survival, resistance can persist despite pathway suppression.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: FcγR engagement on immune effectors activates PI3K signaling in NK/myeloid cells; immune-cell PI3K signatures may rise while tumor remains sensitive via ADCC/ADCP.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Feedback/compensatory activation of PI3K/AKT under HER2 blockade supports survival and is a hallmark of acquired resistance.

KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Mitogenic signaling cascade (RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK) that transduces growth factor receptor inputs into transcriptional programs that drive proliferation and differentiation.
KEGG_MAPK_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: MAPK signaling functions as a major HER2-linked growth pathway supporting tumor proliferation; sustained MAPK signaling is noted as a contributor to reduced response.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: When MAPK/ERK activity is driven by HER2 signaling, it reflects HER2 pathway addiction and predicts sensitivity to HER2 blockade.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: MAPK hyperactivation from alternative RTKs or downstream alterations can maintain proliferation despite HER2 blockade, contributing to trastuzumab resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some HER2+ tumors signal predominantly through PI3K rather than MAPK; low MAPK does not preclude trastuzumab benefit.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low MAPK signatures with parallel survival programs (STAT3/EMT) can still yield primary resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective trastuzumab target engagement reduces HER2-driven RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling, contributing to anti-proliferative effects.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: MAPK suppression can be insufficient if tumors rely on PI3K activation or EMT/stemness programs to survive.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: During early on-treatment dynamics (especially with chemotherapy), stress/inflammatory signaling can transiently elevate MAPK signatures while tumor burden declines.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Reactivation of ERK signaling (e.g., via Notch1–PTEN–ERK axis or RTK switching) is a common adaptive route to trastuzumab resistance.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Gene program reflecting E2F-driven transcription required for S-phase entry and DNA replication, typically downstream of RB phosphorylation and cell-cycle progression.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F target activity serves as a proliferation readout in HER2+ tumors; trastuzumab’s anti-proliferative effects are linked to cell-cycle arrest and reduced proliferation-associated gene expression.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High E2F/proliferation can reflect HER2-driven cell-cycle progression that trastuzumab can suppress via G1 arrest mechanisms.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: E2F-high tumors can be resistant if proliferation is maintained via cyclin E/CDK2 activation or RB-pathway dysfunction that bypasses HER2 control.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lower baseline E2F programs can indicate less cell-cycle bypass and greater vulnerability to HER2 signaling inhibition.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Low proliferation may coexist with intrinsic resistance driven by PI3K/STAT3 signaling, EMT, or immune exclusion.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab increases/stabilizes p27Kip1 and suppresses CDK2 activity, enforcing G1 arrest and decreasing E2F target expression in sensitive HER2+ cells.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: E2F suppression may occur without durable response if residual tumor survives through STAT3/EMT or other survival programs.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Bulk E2F signatures may remain high early (or due to sampling) yet clinical response occurs, particularly with combination chemotherapy plus trastuzumab.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to suppress E2F programs after HER2 blockade (often via cyclin E/CDK2 upregulation) indicates cell-cycle escape and resistance.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Programs governing intrinsic and extrinsic apoptotic signaling that execute regulated cell death through caspase activation and death receptor/mitochondrial pathways.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptotic competence is relevant to HER2 blockade because trastuzumab can sensitize HER2+ tumor cells to apoptotic death, whereas anti-apoptotic signaling is described in resistant states.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: An apoptosis-primed state can increase susceptibility to HER2 signaling withdrawal and Fc-mediated immune cytotoxicity after trastuzumab.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Apoptosis-related transcripts may coexist with dominant anti-apoptotic defenses or ineffective immune killing, limiting response.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors respond mainly through cytostatic G1 arrest rather than strong baseline apoptosis signatures.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low apoptotic priming with strong survival signaling (PI3K/STAT3) reduces cell-death induction and supports resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab can down-regulate anti-apoptotic programs (e.g., BCL-2) and enhance immune killing, increasing apoptosis in responders.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Therapy-induced stress can raise apoptosis markers transiently without eliminating resistant clones sustained by bypass signaling.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Clinical benefit may be dominated by cytostatic arrest with minimal detectable apoptosis induction in bulk transcriptomes.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Resistant tumors often fail to trigger apoptosis after HER2 blockade due to sustained PI3K/STAT3 signaling or EMT/stemness survival programs.

GOBP_FC_GAMMA_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Immune effector signaling initiated by Fcγ receptor engagement on immune cells, triggering activation cascades that promote antibody-dependent cytotoxic and phagocytic responses.
GOBP_FC_GAMMA_RECEPTOR_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Fcγ receptor signaling underlies trastuzumab’s immune mechanism (ADCC) and is described as an important component of effective tumor clearance in HER2+ disease.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Pre-existing activating FcγR signaling competence in NK/monocytes supports trastuzumab ADCC/ADCP and predicts benefit.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: High FcγR signatures can still fail if effector cells are dysfunctional/exhausted or inhibitory FcγR balance dominates.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even with modest FcγR programs, strong HER2 oncogene addiction allows direct signaling blockade to drive response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low FcγR pathway activity (immune-cold tumors) reduces Fc-mediated killing and worsens trastuzumab efficacy.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab Fc engagement activates FcγR signaling on effector cells, driving ADCC/ADCP and contributing to anti-tumor response.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Despite FcγR activation, host genetics (FCGR polymorphisms) or suppressive myeloid programs can blunt killing and yield resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: With deep tumor clearance, less antigen/opsonization can reduce FcγR engagement signatures while sensitivity is evident clinically.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Failure to activate FcγR programs after dosing (poor antibody exposure or low effector infiltration) is consistent with non-response.

KEGG_NATURAL_KILLER_CELL_MEDIATED_CYTOTO.description: NK cell activation and cytotoxic effector mechanisms (including perforin/granzyme-mediated killing) that eliminate antibody-opsonized target cells.
KEGG_NATURAL_KILLER_CELL_MEDIATED_CYTOTO.interpretation: NK-mediated cytotoxicity is mechanistically tied to trastuzumab-driven ADCC and is described as correlating with response when robust immune activation is present.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: NK cytotoxicity programs support trastuzumab-mediated ADCC and correlate with better responses in HER2+ breast cancer.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NK-high tumors can remain resistant if immunosuppressive signals or FcγR inhibitory balance blocks effective ADCC.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can still respond via direct HER2 blockade, especially with concomitant chemotherapy, even when NK activity is low.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low NK cytotoxicity reduces the immune effector contribution to trastuzumab activity, increasing likelihood of resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab opsonization promotes NK activation and cytotoxic killing of HER2+ cells, increasing NK pathway activity in responders.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: NK pathways may activate but be insufficient if tumor uses strong intrinsic resistance (PI3K/EMT) or immune suppression persists.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Successful tumor debulking can reduce ongoing NK engagement signatures while clinical sensitivity remains.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low NK cytotoxicity after treatment indicates poor immune effector recruitment/activation and supports resistance.

HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.description: Gene program reflecting angiogenic signaling and neovascularization processes that support tumor perfusion, growth, and progression.
HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.interpretation: Angiogenesis is described as a tumor-supportive process that can be inhibited by trastuzumab and may counteract therapy when high.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: If angiogenesis is driven by HER2 signaling (HER2→HIF-1/VEGF), HER2 blockade can reduce VEGF output and contribute to response.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Angiogenesis driven by hypoxia/inflammatory cues can persist despite HER2 blockade, supporting progression and resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low baseline angiogenic signaling can reflect less aggressive vascular remodeling and may associate with better trastuzumab response.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may be resistant through PI3K/EMT/STAT3 routes even if angiogenesis programs are low.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trastuzumab can decrease HER2-driven VEGF expression and exert anti-angiogenic effects, aiding tumor control in responders.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Angiogenesis signatures may fall without durable response if intrinsic tumor survival pathways remain dominant.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Inflammatory immune influx during effective therapy can raise angiogenesis-related transcripts (wound-healing programs) despite overall sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Compensatory VEGF/angiogenic program upregulation under HER2 blockade can support acquired resistance and progression.

HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING.description: Developmental signaling pathway controlling cell fate, stemness, and survival via NOTCH receptor activation and downstream transcriptional programs.
HALLMARK_NOTCH_SIGNALING.interpretation: Notch signaling is described as a compensatory survival/stemness pathway that can increase after HER2 blockade and contribute to resistance biology.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Notch activity is more often linked to stemness and resistance; sensitivity with Notch-high tumors would usually require dominant HER2 addiction overriding Notch-mediated survival.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Notch/Jagged programs promote cancer stem cell maintenance and have been implicated in trastuzumab resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low Notch signaling reduces stemness-associated bypass survival, supporting trastuzumab sensitivity in HER2-addicted tumors.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with low Notch, resistance can occur via PI3K activation or immune/PK limitations.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Notch may rise as an adaptive response even in partial responders; clinical benefit can still occur before resistant clones dominate.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Therapy-induced Jagged/Notch activation (often coupled to IL-6/STAT3) is reported as a route to acquired trastuzumab resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Notch suppression may accompany effective tumor control (reduced stem-like fraction) in responders, though not a primary direct effect of trastuzumab.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Notch can be low yet resistance persists via PI3K/EMT; thus Notch downregulation alone is not sufficient for response.

HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.description: Cytokine-driven signaling axis in which IL-6 activates JAK kinases and STAT3 transcriptional programs that promote inflammation, survival, and immune regulation.
HALLMARK_IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING.interpretation: IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling is described as implicated in resistance and survival programs (often linked with Notch/STAT3 and inflammatory signaling) in the trastuzumab context.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Baseline IL-6/STAT3 inflammation is generally pro-survival and predicts resistance; sensitivity would typically require strong HER2 addiction and/or immune-effective context overcoming STAT3 signaling.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: IL-6–JAK–STAT3 inflammatory loops expand stem-like cells and promote trastuzumab resistance in HER2+ breast cancer.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low IL-6/STAT3 activity reduces pro-survival inflammation and stemness programs, supporting trastuzumab responsiveness.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can remain resistant through PI3K activation or EMT even if IL-6/STAT3 signaling is low.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: STAT3 can activate as a stress response during treatment; transient STAT3 elevation may not prevent short-term clinical benefit in some patients.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Feedback activation of STAT3 and IL-6 loops under HER2 blockade is a documented mechanism of acquired trastuzumab resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective therapy can reduce tumor-derived IL-6 signaling and dampen STAT3 programs alongside tumor regression.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even if IL-6/STAT3 programs diminish, resistance may persist via PI3K or EMT-driven survival.

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: Phenotypic transition program involving loss of epithelial features and gain of mesenchymal traits, associated with invasiveness, stem-like behavior, and therapy resistance.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation: EMT is described as linked to a stem-like, trastuzumab-resistant phenotype and is noted as relevant even if not a direct trastuzumab target pathway.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: EMT-high states often reduce HER2 dependence and immune susceptibility; sensitivity would typically require concurrent strong HER2 amplification and effective immune engagement.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: EMT programs are repeatedly linked to primary resistance to trastuzumab and to acquisition of resistant phenotypes.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: An epithelial phenotype (low EMT) is consistent with HER2-driven, trastuzumab-responsive disease and less stemness/bypass signaling.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can be epithelial yet resistant via PI3K activation, cyclin E/CDK2 escape, or limited immune effector activity.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: EMT signatures may rise transiently during remodeling/inflammation even in responders, but sustained EMT is more typical of resistance.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Chronic trastuzumab pressure can select for EMT/mesenchymal states (especially with PTEN loss), driving acquired resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Effective therapy can reduce EMT programs by shrinking invasive/mesenchymal subclones, supporting sensitivity.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: EMT can be low yet resistance persists via PI3K/STAT3/cell-cycle escape mechanisms; EMT suppression alone is not sufficient for response.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High FCGR3A (CD16) expression on NK cells is stated to correlate with trastuzumab sensitivity, consistent with effective ADCC as a key mechanism.
p27^Kip1 (CDKN1B) upregulation is described as enforcing G1 arrest after trastuzumab exposure; baseline association with response is noted via CDK inhibitor/apoptotic context.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Activating mutations in PIK3CA are stated to reactivate PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of HER2 and confer trastuzumab resistance.
STAT3-mediated survival/anti-apoptotic signaling is described as becoming upregulated in resistant contexts (often linked to Notch/inflammatory signaling).
Notch signaling (including Notch1) is described as a compensatory pathway that can increase after HER2 blockade and promote survival/stemness and resistance.
Jagged1 (JAG1) is described as part of a Jagged1/Notch1 axis that can become upregulated following HER2 blockade and contribute to resistance biology.
Activation of HER3 (ERBB3) is described as providing bypass proliferative/survival signaling that can undermine trastuzumab effects.
Increased signaling through EGFR is described as an alternate receptor tyrosine kinase input that can provide bypass growth signals and contribute to resistance.
IGF1R signaling is described as a bypass pathway that can engage alternate proliferation/survival signals and reduce trastuzumab effectiveness.
SRC kinase signaling is described as frequently upregulated in resistant cells as part of bypass/survival signaling downstream of RTK cross-talk.
IL-6/JAK-STAT signaling is described as implicated in resistance and survival/inflammatory programs (linked to Notch/STAT3 context).
MET is described as a growth factor cross-talk RTK whose increased signaling can engage bypass pathways that undermine trastuzumab effects.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss of PTEN is stated to reactivate PI3K/AKT signaling and confer trastuzumab resistance.
Resistant cells are described as often losing p27 (CDKN1B), allowing cell-cycle progression despite trastuzumab-associated arrest mechanisms.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Positive (ERBB2-amplified) Breast C: Trastuzumab is effective only in tumors overexpressing HER2 (approx. 15–20% of breast cancers). It improves outcomes in both hormone receptor–positive (often “Luminal B HER2+”) and hormone receptor–negative HER2+ tumors.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-Negative Subtypes (TNBC, Luminal A/: Trastuzumab is not indicated because the target is absent. Clinical trials show no benefit in pure HER2-negative disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-Mutated Cancers: There is no specific role for trastuzumab based on BRCA status. HER2+ cancers should be treated with HER2-targeted therapy regardless of BRCA, and BRCA-mutant TNBC are managed with platinum/PARP inhibitors rather than trastuzumab.

notes: No absolute contraindications were stated; key safety issues described include cardiotoxicity (LVEF decline/heart failure risk), infusion reactions, embryo-fetal toxicity, and pulmonary toxicity.
